candidates.content_text:
The Opportunity:
Maitland City Council's Pathways program is a fantastic way to kick-start your career and gain professional experience in local government!
Commencing in January 2027, for a period of two years, we have two exciting opportunities for Graduate Civil Engineers to join our organisation.
In this role, you will undertake a graduate program developed specifically for you, giving you exposure to a range of civil engineering functions for the investigation and delivery of civil and recreation infrastructure projects undertaken by Council. These duties are going to help you develop a solid foundation to your civil engineering career.
About you:
To be successful in this role you will possess:
- Degree level qualifications in Civil engineering in the previous two years or completion of degree by January 2027
- Contemporary industry knowledge of civil engineering areas
- Experience and understanding in project support and the research, analysis and presentation of information
- Current Class C driver's licence
Benefits:
This Graduate position is temporary full time (two-year contract) with a commencing salary of $1,414.58 weekly, plus 12% superannuation. Graduates will also have access to Council's great staff benefits including:
- Flexible work arrangements
- One extra week of "My Leave" a year (to use how you like!)
- Ongoing training and development
- Fitness Passport
- Healthy Employee Program
To apply:
To apply for this opportunity, please click 'Apply Now' and submit your resume and cover letter.
Questions:
To viw the role charter click 'Apply Now'. If after reading the role charter you have any questions, please contact the recruitment team at Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au
More information regarding Council's Pathways Program can be viewed via https://www.maitland.nsw.gov.au/pathways-program.
Applications close: Sunday 25th October 2027
Only candidates with current Australian work rights (Australian citizens, permanent residents, NZ citizens with a current passport, valid work visa) will be considered.
What happens next?
Once applications close, we will review all candidates' details against the role requirements and will be back in touch with you to advise the status of your application.
Please note, prior to an offer of employment being made, recommended candidates will be required to undertake a medical assessment (including drug and alcohol testing). Council also completes a range of other pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, psychometric testing or a criminal history check. For more information about the recruitment process, visit the "Jobs at Council" page on our website.
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
Maitland City Council is dedicated to providing a workplace that is inclusive and supportive and is reflective of the diverse community we serve. We support equal opportunities for all employees, and encourage applications from people from all cultures, nationalities, identities, and abilities. We believe all employees have the right to feel valued, respected and heard. If you have any special considerations or accessibility requirements, please let us know in the recruitment process how we are able to meet your needs.
 If you require special assistance, or have any questions about the recruitment process please contact us for a confidential conversation (Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au)

About the role
Ground Civil is seeking an experienced Civil Designer to join our West Perth office, with strong experience in subdivision and land development design.
You will work on a variety of civil and land development projects across Western Australia, taking designs from initial concept through detailed design and authority approval. The role will suit a practical designer who is confident in Civil 3D and can work independently while collaborating closely with our engineering team.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare subdivision and land development designs using AutoCAD Civil 3D
- Design roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage, sewer and water infrastructure
- Prepare detailed design and construction drawings
- Develop Civil 3D surfaces, alignments, profiles, corridors and earthworks models
- Coordinate designs with surveyors, engineers and other consultants
- Assist with local government, Water Corporation and other authority approvals
- Respond to design review comments and coordinate amendments through to approval
- Ensure designs and documentation are accurate, practical and compliant with applicable standards
About you
- Demonstrated civil design experience in subdivision and land development
- Strong proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D
- Practical experience in road, drainage, earthworks and utility design
- Australian civil design experience
- WA subdivision and land development experience will be highly regarded
- Familiarity with WA approval processes and relevant authority requirements will be highly regarded
- Ability to work independently and manage design tasks efficiently
- Strong attention to detail and ability to produce high-quality construction documentation
- Good communication and coordination skills
Why join Ground Civil?
- Work directly on a diverse range of subdivision and land development projects
- Be involved across the design process rather than working on only one component
- Work closely with experienced engineers in our West Perth office
- Opportunity to take ownership of designs and develop broader project experience
- Professional and supportive small-team environment

candidates.content_text:
Civil Designer, 12d Modeller - Roads & Highways | Sunshine Coast
Help shape the future of transport infrastructure across Southeast Queensland.
At Aurecon, we're delivering some of Queensland's most important roads and highways projects. We're looking for a Civil Designer / 12D Modeller to join our Roads team and contribute to the design and delivery of TMR and transport infrastructure projects across the region.
This role is ideally based on the Sunshine Coast, with opportunities for candidates across Southeast Queensland who are open to working from or relocating to the region.
Whether you're an experienced designer or an emerging professional with strong 12D capabilities, we'd love to hear from you.
What you'll do
- Prepare civil road designs and 12D models for transport infrastructure projects
- Work closely with engineers, project managers and other design professionals
- Support the delivery of TMR and Main Roads projects across Southeast Queensland
- Produce high-quality design documentation and technical deliverables
- Contribute to innovative, practical and sustainable infrastructure solutions
What you'll bring
- Experience in civil design and/or 12D modelling within roads and highways projects
- Exposure to TMR/Main Roads projects and standards
- Strong technical skills and attention to detail
- Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
- Relevant experience in transport infrastructure, road design or civil engineering projects
- Knowledge of Queensland road design standards and practices
How we support your growth
We believe your career should be a rewarding adventure. You will tackle some of the world's most complex infrastructure challenges, in an environment that supports your ambitions, where we hold ourselves, and each other, to the highest standards. Recognised by the AFR as a Best Place to Work in 2026, we embrace diverse perspectives, giving you the opportunity to make a real impact. 
Who we are 
We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities. They are the ones who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is our purpose. Bringing ideas to life. This is The Aurecon Way. 
Ready for your next adventure? 
If this sounds like your next step, we'd love to hear from you. We value diverse experiences and welcome applications for part-time or flexible working arrangements. 
Our hiring decisions are made by people, not AI. We're most interested in your individual thinking and experiences-so please ensure your application reflects your authentic perspective.

 WGA, an AtkinsRéalis company, is a multidisciplinary engineering and project management consultancy delivering complex infrastructure projects across Australia and New Zealand.  - Qualification in Civil Engineering. Diploma in Civil Design or equivalent

 At WGA, we believe a diverse workplace fosters unique and progressive ideas and drives our culture of learning and knowledge sharing. Join us and advance your career while enjoying the unique benefits and opportunities that come with being part of a local team with global reach.

Build More. Build Your Career.
Ready to kick-start your engineering career on some of Southeast Queensland’s most exciting infrastructure projects?
Seymour Whyte's Graduate Program gives ambitious engineering graduates the opportunity to work on major projects, take on real responsibility from day one, and develop the technical, commercial and leadership skills needed for a successful career in construction.
Through our structured two-year development program, you'll gain hands-on experience across major civil infrastructure projects, work alongside industry leaders, receive dedicated mentoring and build the skills and confidence to accelerate your career.  You'll be trusted with real responsibility, supported to grow and given the opportunity to make a genuine impact while helping deliver infrastructure that connects communities.
About the Project
We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to join our Beerburrum to Nambour (B2N) Rail Upgrade project.
This a major infrastructure project transforming the North Coast Line on the Sunshine Coast. The project includes rail duplication, new and upgraded transport infrastructure, improved road overpasses and enhanced signalling systems, all aimed at increasing capacity and reliability across the network. Once complete, B2N will deliver faster and more efficient travel while improving connections between the Sunshine Coast, Moreton Bay and Brisbane, creating lasting benefits for local communities and the region.
Why Join Seymour Whyte?
At Seymour Whyte, we believe the best way to learn is by doing. Our structured Graduate Development Program is designed to fast-track your career through hands-on project experience, mentoring from industry leaders and tailored professional development opportunities.
From day one, you'll be embedded in a live project team, contributing to the delivery of major infrastructure projects that shape communities across Australia. You'll gain exposure to a range of disciplines, build your technical and commercial acumen and develop the confidence to take ownership of meaningful work early in your career.
Throughout the program, you'll be supported by experienced mentors, participate in structured development workshops, and connect with a national network of graduates and professionals who are invested in your success.
What's in it for you?
- Work on a landmark civil infrastructure project from day one
- Gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery
- Receive structured mentoring, coaching and development support
- Learn from experienced industry leaders and subject matter experts
- Build a strong professional network across projects and regions
- Be part of a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
- Access career opportunities within the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction, infrastructure and concessions
Whether your passion lies in construction delivery, engineering, project management or leadership, our Graduate Development Program will provide the foundation, support and opportunities to help you build a rewarding and long-term career with Seymour Whyte.
To learn more about our Graduate Program, click here.
About You
You're in your final year of a Bachelor of Civil Engineering and ready to turn everything you've learned into real-world experience on major infrastructure projects.
Whether you've gained experience through an internship, vacation work, industry placement or part-time employment, you're eager to learn, build your skills and make a meaningful contribution from day one.
We're looking for graduates who are curious, motivated and excited about a career in civil construction.
You'll bring:
- Final-year studies in a Bachelor of Civil Engineering
- Practical experience through internships, vacation programs, placements or other employment
- A genuine passion for civil construction and infrastructure projects
- A positive attitude and willingness to learn from experienced industry professionals
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A commitment to safety, collaboration and creating a positive team culture
- Flexibility to travel or relocate as opportunities arise throughout your career
Most importantly, you're ready to take the next step, embrace new challenges and build a rewarding career delivering projects that make a lasting impact on communities across Australia.
Seymour Whyte Benefits
- Employee recognition and awards that celebrate contribution and achievement
- An employee share program, providing the opportunity to invest in the long-term success of the business
- Birthday leave, because celebrating life's milestones matters
- The option to purchase additional leave to support travel, study or personal commitments
- Fitness and wellbeing discounts through WHEREFIT (gym memberships, meal plans and fitness brands)
- Travel, retail, lifestyle and wellness discounts
- Workplace banking benefits and everyday financial savings through CommBank and Flare
Seymour Whyte is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, including veterans.
Our commitment to an equitable construction industry extends to an inclusive culture that embraces our differences and gives everyone the opportunity to grow and be equally valued. We're unified in our direction toward having a workplace that is balanced and fair for all.
Next Steps:
- Submit your CV online to apply for this role
- All successful applicants will be required to undergo a pre-employment medical and criminal history check
- Applications will only be accepted from candidates who have the right to work in Australia
To learn more about us, visit www.seymourwhyte.com.au

About us
Brisbane Truss & Timber is a growing timber truss and wall frame manufacturer based in Bundamba, running the latest Pryda design software and automated production equipment. We supply builders across South East Queensland and we're building a team that can keep up with demand.
About the Role
As a Civil Engineer Draftsperson, you will be responsible for preparing, developing and
modifying technical drawings and documentation associated with civil, structural and timber
construction projects.
Working closely with engineers, estimators, builders and other members of the design team, you
will assist in translating architectural and engineering requirements into accurate construction
drawings and documentation.
Key Responsibilities
- Prepare detailed civil, structural and construction drawings using Pryda
drafting software.
- Develop drawings and technical documentation for roof trusses, wall frames, floor
systems and related structural timber solutions.
- Interpret architectural plans, engineering drawings, specifications and project
requirements.
- Prepare detailed layouts, plans, elevations, sections and construction details.
- Review drawings for accuracy, completeness and compliance with project specifications.
- Modify and update drawings in accordance with engineering and design changes.
- Liaise with engineers, builders, estimators and project personnel to resolve drafting and design issues.
- Assist with estimating and design documentation for residential and commercial construction projects.
- Maintain accurate drawing registers, revisions and project documentation.
- Ensure drafting work is completed accurately and within agreed project timeframes.
- Assist the wider design team with technical documentation and project coordination as required.
Skills & Experience
The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Relevant qualifications in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering Drafting, Engineering
- Drafting, Civil Construction Design or a related discipline.
- Previous experience in a civil/structural drafting or engineering environment.
- Strong knowledge of technical drawing principles and construction documentation.
- Proficiency in Pryda/MiTech/CAD and relevant drafting/design software.
- Ability to interpret architectural, engineering and construction drawings.
- Understanding of structural and construction principles.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a small technical team.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills.
- Experience in the timber, building or construction industry will be highly regarded.
What's of offer
- Competitive salary based on experience
- Stable, growing local manufacturer — not a corporate machine, decisions get made fast
- Modern software and equipment
- On-site parking at our Bundamba facility, easy access from Ipswich Motorway

candidates.content_text:
Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting! 
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career? 
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry. 
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Structural Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland. 
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn. 
Why you’ll love working here 
Start building your career   Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical Structural drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters. 
Work on real projects   Go beyond the classroom and see how structural engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery. 
Learn from experienced people   Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow. 
Be part of a great team   Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do. 
Work in Fortitude Valley   Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity  
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to: 
- Assist with preparing structural drawings, plans and project documentation. 
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings. 
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes. 
- Develop your understanding of how structural engineering projects are designed and delivered. 
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements. 
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members. 
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop. 
About you: 
You could be a great fit if you are: 
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver, or currently studying Residential Drafting, or an equivalent qualification at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in structural drafting, design and engineering. 
- Curious and keen to learn new skills. 
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work. 
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback. 
- Reliable, organised and willing to have a go at new challenges. 
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team. 
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident. 
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career. 
What’s in it for you? 
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development. 
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution. 
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs. 
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events. 
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program. 
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy. 
About STP Consultants  
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. 
We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take. 
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other. 
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes. 
Ready to get started?   
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you. 
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter. 
In your cover letter, tell us: 
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in structural drafting.   
2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants. 
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

- Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving abilities.

To gain a better understanding of the role or to discuss the position qualification requirements in detail, please call Chris Edwards, Manager Project Delivery and Engineering on (08) 9956 6949.

The successful applicant will ideally hold a Degree in Civil Engineering or Design or progressing towards a Degree. Applicants with significant experience in the design and preparation of civil drawings in 12D and/or AutoCAD including project cost estimating will also be considered.
Completion of a pre-employment medical including alcohol and other substances testing is required of all positions at the City.
Remuneration and benefits:
This position offers a salary starting from $92,692 per annum, commensurate with the successful applicant’s knowledge, skills, experience and qualifications.

- Up to 21% Superannuation (with superannuation co-contribution scheme)
- 22 Annual Leave days per annum
- Health & Wellbeing Program
- Flexible working arrangements
- Career opportunities

With a growing population of over 41,000 people it offers a wide range of services and activities. Geraldton is recognised as one of WA's key growth areas and the opportunities in this regional city are plentiful. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer with strong commitment to fitness for work and safety in the workplace.
Interested in applying?
Visit the City’s website: www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/ to apply for this position.

- A current resume
- A written response (maximum 1250 characters per criteria) addressing the following selection criteria inclusive of examples to support your claims:
i. Experience in investigations and the preparation of engineering planning reports
ii. Sound understanding of civil engineering principles and practices, with a developing knowledge of development engineering, subdivision and infrastructure assets

candidates.content_text:
ABOUT US
Ertech is a proudly employee-owned Australian civil and electrical construction company, delivering high-quality services across the Transport, Infrastructure, Resources, and Defence sectors. We partner with clients in both the public and private sectors, including state and federal governments. Since our humble beginnings in 1981, we’ve built a strong reputation for the quality of our work and the long-term relationships we foster — all driven by our core values of collaboration, courage, and authenticity.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
We are currently seeking an experienced Project Engineer (Civil) to join our Resources team, supporting the delivery of Civil and Electrical construction scopes on the Wheatstone NRU Thermal Oxidiser (TOX) Project.
As the Project Engineer, you will play a key role in the successful delivery of civil construction activities, providing technical and project support while ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in line with project requirements, schedule and budget.
Other key responsibilities include, but not limited to:
- Coordinate daily construction activities to achieve project scope, schedule and budget requirements.
- Develop and monitor construction programs, key milestones, productivity and critical path activities.
- Review drawings, specifications and technical documentation to ensure works meet project and design requirements.
- Prepare methodologies, ITPs, SWMS and other engineering documentation.
- Manage RFIs, design clarifications and technical queries with relevant stakeholders.
- Forecast labour, plant, materials and subcontractor requirements.
- Identify project risks, constraints and potential delays, implementing mitigation and recovery strategies.
- Verify quantities, completed works and progress claims.
- Support project reporting, documentation and contractual deliverables.
To be successful, you will have experience and demonstrate capability in the following:
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering.
- Minimum 5 years’ experience in civil construction project delivery.
- Experience delivering works within brownfield industrial or resources environments.
- Strong knowledge of concrete, foundations, earthworks and underground services.
- Experience in contract administration and commercial management.
- Proven ability to coordinate multiple work fronts and subcontractors.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Primavera P6 and project management systems.
- Construction White Card (CPCWHS1001 – Prepare to work safely in the construction industry).
- Ability to obtain a National Police Clearance.
- Valid Australian working rights.
WHY JOIN ERTECH?
- Competitive remuneration, including site uplift
- Choice of a 2:2 or 2:1 roster to suit your lifestyle
- Supportive, team-oriented culture where collaboration and respect are valued 
- Play a key role in shaping the growth and success of our projects
- Career development and progression opportunities, annual performance development plans.
- Access to great benefits, including: 
- Discounted Private Health Insurance (HBF & Medibank)
- Annual flu vaccinations 
- Novated leasing options through Paywise
- Service recognition and milestone rewards 
- Employee Referral Program incentives 
OUR CULTURE
At Ertech, our people are fundamental to our success. We're focused on creating an inclusive workplace, with the right people in the right roles, who are engaged, empowered, and appropriately rewarded. Ertech will provide you with the chance to be a part of great team, meet new people and gain experience with an industry leader who puts safety first. 
DIVERSITY & INCLUSION
We value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of all people and actively encourage applications from First Nations peoples, all genders, culturally and linguistically diverse individuals, people with disability, LGBTQIA+ community members, and veterans of the Australian Defence Force.
Ertech is a proud Veteran Employment supporter. We recognise the valuable skills and leadership that veterans bring to our industry and welcome their applications at all levels of the business. Even if you don’t meet every requirement listed, we encourage you to apply and bring your strengths to our team.
HOW TO APPLY
Click "Apply" on this job advertisement, which will direct you to Ertech's application portal. Simply follow the steps outlined on the portal to complete your application.
This is an incredible opportunity! If you are looking for a position in an environment in which you can flourish whilst building your career, there is no better time to join the Ertech Team than now!
*Please note: This role is being sourced through Ertech directly and we will not accept applications via external recruitment agencies.

Bring infrastructure projects to life through innovative design, collaboration and technical engineering expertise.
Position details

About the Opportunity
Join Council’s Engineering Development & Delivery Branch and help shape practical infrastructure outcomes for the Mildura region. In this role, you will investigate, design and estimate road, drainage and other capital works projects, using tools such as AutoCAD and Civil 3D while collaborating with internal teams, authorities and community stakeholders. This is an excellent opportunity to apply your technical and problem-solving skills across varied projects that deliver lasting value for our community.
What you will bring

- Demonstrated working knowledge of the design of road and drainage works.
- Demonstrated working knowledge of AutoCAD and Civil 3D, with proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.
- Demonstrated ability to investigate, problem solve and provide solutions to Civil Engineering issues.
- Ability to liaise effectively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.
- A current Driver’s Licence.
- Hold a current satisfactory Police Check or ability to obtain one prior to commencement.
Salary and conditions
The position is classified within Band 5 of Council’s Current Enterprise Agreement commencing at $80,057.64 per annum plus statutory superannuation.
Benefits 
As an employee you will have access to benefits such as:
- Monthly  Accrued Day Off 
- Flexible Work Arrangements (Flextime, Purchase of Additional Leave)
- Access to Flare Employee Benefits for savings on everyday living
- Financial recognition upon successful annual performance review, including either progression through banding structure or end-of-band bonus payment.

- Discounted Health Insurance and Gym Memberships
- Employee Assistance Program: Free Counselling for Employees and Immediate Family Members

For a full list of councils benefits please visit our website: https://www.mildura.vic.gov.au/Council/Careers/Employee-Benefits
Mildura Rural City Council is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building a culture that values diversity. We encourage applications from individuals of all ages, backgrounds and identities.
We encourage people with a disability, lived experience of disability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders and people from culturally diverse backgrounds to apply for this position.
All applicants must have the right to work in Australia and will need to provide a Police Check prior to commencing employment.
Mildura Rural City Council is a Child Safe organisation and as such, applicants may be required to hold a Working with Children Check. Applicants may also be required to undergo a pre-employment medical check as per the requirements of the role.
About our organisation
Mildura Rural City Council is a dynamic local government organisation that provides 100+ different services, facilities, programs and infrastructure to a resident base of 56,000+. Our workforce of 600+ employees support our community and help make our region a great place to live, work, play and visit. As an employer of choice and a Gold Award winner in the Business Excellence Awards, we are committed to innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement. Learn more about our organisation at www.mildura.vic.gov.au
About our region
Mildura Rural City covers almost 10 per cent of the state of Victoria and shares borders with both New South Wales and South Australia. The region is home to Mildura - a vibrant city of 35,000+ people - and a range of smaller townships and rural communities spread across 22,000 square kilometres.
Only a short flight from three capital cities, Mildura boasts quality services, exciting attractions, diverse industries and a strong community spirit. There are fantastic professional, cultural, social, sporting and educational opportunities on offer. Learn more about our region at www.visitmildura.com.au

candidates.content_text:
Your Role 
As a Civil Engineer in the Army Reserve, you’ll get to use your existing qualifications in exciting new ways, applying your specialist skills to dynamic military environments. You’ll plan, design, coordinate, control and deliver a range of infrastructure engineering projects. 
This is a great opportunity to challenge yourself and work in exciting new environments, without compromising your current career goals.  
 Your duties may include: 
- aiding the community in humanitarian efforts 
- construction of field defences and obstacles 
- military and training duties 
- project managing the construction, repair and maintenance of roads, airfields, sea terminals, railways, buildings and bridges 
- providing terrain assessment advice 
- provision of construction materials and essential services such as water, electricity, and sewerage disposal 
- general soldiering duties, such as manning defensive positions, patrolling, traffic control, navigation, and camouflaging of vehicles and field equipment. 
Why join the Army Reserve?  
If you're looking for a new challenge, the Army Reserve could be for you. You'll enjoy the satisfaction of giving something back to Australia, while benefitting from:  
- Rewarding work that can be in complete contrast to your day job   
- Tax-free daily pay  
- Free healthcare and accommodation whilst on exercise or deployment  
- A flexible time commitment, ranging from a couple of weeks up to 150 days, with the potential to extend to 200 days  
- Easy to fit into your lifestyle with the option to work close to home   
- Comprehensive training   
- A supportive team environment  
- Can volunteer to deploy overseas 
- Friendships that last a lifetime  
- No minimum period of service, allowing you to leave and come back to the Army Reserve whenever you like 
Boost Your Income 
On completion of your initial military and employment training, you could earn at least $283/day tax-free. 
The pay you receive in the Army Reserve goes straight into your pocket with no deductions for tax, and it increases as you gain seniority and experience. Additional amounts are paid for time spent on exercises and deployments. 
Eligibility:
For this role, you must:  
- Be at least 17 at the time of enlistment and an Australian Citizen.  
- If you are not an Australian Citizen you may still be eligible to join the ADF if you meet certain criteria, please visit the ADF Careers Eligibility Page for more details  
- Be reasonably fit and healthy. Keeping fit is a big part of joining the ADF. You’ll need to pass a physical fitness test before you join, but don’t worry, we'll give you tips to help you prepare.  
- Be able to successfully obtain a security clearance. 
- Hold a Bachelor of Civil Engineering or a related discipline 
- Have had training in a branch of engineering with the practical experience required for graduate membership of the Institution of Engineers Australia (IEAust), or another chartered institution of similar status. 
Apply Now  
Apply today or request more information by calling 13 19 01 or emailing  applications@adfcareers.gov.au.

Life at Fulton Hogan is about making the most of opportunities, taking responsibility, and making it happen. We appreciate our peoples' courage, curiosity and unique perspectives, and look to collaborate as much as possible to explore safer, smarter and more efficient ways of working in this rapidly changing world. We don't stand still - there are always opportunities to do more and do better.
- Keen to progress your career? Take full advantage of our tailored training, leadership, and mentoring programs; or leverage our partnerships with industry association such as Engineers Australia, Chartered Accountants, CPA Australia, Infrastructure Sustainability Council, The National Association of Women in Construction, plus many more.

We offer great benefits, including corporate health and fitness programs, health insurance discounts, personal banking support, a range of retailer discounts, up to 18 weeks paid primary carers parental leave and up to 10 days paid secondary carers leave, access to our Employee Assistance Program (including your immediate family), and the option to take more time for yourself throughout the year with our Purchase Leave Policy.
- Want to help us better the communities we live and work in? Our purpose of creating, connecting, and caring for communities is more than a saying to us - it's a way of thinking, working, and living because we're locals too, and seek to give back in ways that strengthen and build resilient communities. We do this because we genuinely care, enjoy what we do, and even manage to have some fun along the way! You'll find us partnering with local and national community groups, like Clontarf Foundation and Black Dog Institute, in addition to indigenous groups and social enterprises, to ensure that our good work positively impacts and brings about sustainable change within our industry.
- Do we offer a 'competitive' salary package? Of course! Speak to our Talent Acquisition or People & Culture team to learn more.
What's on offer?
With the continued growth and diversification of our business, we are looking to appoint a Civil Estimator to join our Northern Region (QLD) Infrastructure business based in Eight Mile Plains.
Fulton Hogan is offering an exciting career path for a Civil Construction Professional to become an established estimator within the wider Fulton Hogan Infrastructure Services business. Key clients include National Defence, State Government, Local Government and the private sector throughout Queensland. 
You will be provided with direct support from the local business and formal mentoring from the National Civil Estimating Manager to develop and grow your estimating prowess and unlock your full potential. We will provide initial and ongoing training in the use of Expert Estimator Genesis.
You may be an existing Estimator, a Project Engineer or a Civil construction professional seeking a new career path without the rigorous demands of site-based roles. Substantial delivery phase and demonstrated site experience is essential to this role. You will have great communication skills with a good rapport with clients, subcontractors, and suppliers across the industry and enjoy working in a team environment. 
Reporting directly to the FHI Northern Sales & Tendering Manager you will be responsible for:
- Managing the tender process from start to finish including ensuring all elements of the tender are considered by the appropriate stakeholders and completed within the allotted time.
- Reviewing all tender documentation including specifications, quality, safety, and other requirements, as well as attending onsite tender briefings as required from time to time.
- Developing a winning construction methodology, including staging plans and verifying client schedules, programming the scope of works according to the construction methodology, assessing duration and productivity, and conducting win/loss reporting.
- Ensuring resource rates used are based on market rates & conditions, coordinating and sending out subcontractor/supply pricing packages, and performing overall quote analysis.
- Undertaking first principals estimates for various elements of civil construction, in conjunction with subcontractor pricing to ensure best for project outcomes
- Preparing detailed cost reports, summaries, and presentations for internal stakeholders and clients, providing presentations on project feasibility, budget adherence, innovations and cost-savings.
 To be successful we are seeking:
- Intermediate knowledge within the Civil Construction Industry.
- Demonstrated experience and technical knowledge of civil infrastructure projects, pricing from first principles and/or delivering projects on site with ambitions to transition into a full-time Civil Estimator role.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills including writing.
- Ability to construct detailed Construction Programs in MS Project or similar.
- Detailed knowledge of estimating software such as Expert Estimator or equivalent estimating packages will be highly regarded, but not essential.
 This position may require ad hoc travel.
Our people share the same set of values that keep us REAL. Respect, Energy and Effort, Attitude and Leadership encapsulate what we stand for at Fulton Hogan and encourage us to foster a diverse and inclusive culture where we listen to, care for, celebrate, and respect everyone.
We are committed to reconciliation and building and nurturing respectful relationships with First Nations peoples. Through our First Nations Engagement Strategy and Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP), we aim to promote opportunities, cultural understanding and partnerships that celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of Indigenous communities.
If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position. If you're not sure that you meet 100% of the selection criteria, that's okay, we would still like to hear from you and potentially discuss how your skills could be utilised at Fulton Hogan.
For over 90 years, Fulton Hogan has been delivering high-quality infrastructure to improve the lives of people every day. Our 10,000+ team works in every kind of weather and environment, creating, connecting, and caring for communities across Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific.

Doolee is a leading civil construction company operating across Australia, with offices in WA and NSW, delivering complex, high-quality infrastructure projects across a diverse range of sectors. We are currently seeking a skilled and experienced Civil Engineer to join our dynamic team and contribute to the successful delivery of our projects.
Position Overview
As a Civil Engineer, you will be responsible for planning, designing, organising and overseeing civil engineering and construction projects from planning through to delivery. You will provide technical engineering expertise across project design, construction methodologies, materials, quality standards, cost management and site coordination, working closely with project managers, site personnel, subcontractors, consultants and clients to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with engineering requirements, specifications and Australian Standards.
Key Responsibilities
- Plan, design, organise and oversee the construction and delivery of civil engineering and infrastructure projects.
- Review, interpret and prepare engineering drawings, plans, specifications, construction methods and procedures.
- Organise and coordinate site labour, construction materials, plant and equipment to support the efficient delivery of project works.
- Establish and maintain detailed programs for the coordination of site activities, resources and construction works.
- Undertake site inspections, investigations and assessments to determine project requirements, site conditions and construction feasibility.
- Study engineering drawings and specifications to assist with cost estimates, quantity measurements, cost plans and budgetary control.
- Monitor project costs, construction progress and resource requirements, identifying potential cost impacts and delays.
- Monitor changes to designs and assess their impact on project costs, construction methodology, program and resources.
- Measure, value and assist with the negotiation and management of variations to designs, scope and construction works.
- Coordinate with project managers, engineers, supervisors, subcontractors, consultants and clients to ensure effective project delivery.
- Assist with the design and development of civil infrastructure, including earthworks, roads, drainage, pavements and associated civil works.
- Ensure engineering and construction activities comply with relevant Australian Standards, legislation, safety requirements and project specifications.
- Identify project risks, construction issues and opportunities for improvement and implement appropriate engineering and corrective solutions.
- Provide technical support throughout the project lifecycle, from planning and design through to construction and completion.
Qualifications and Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a relevant engineering discipline.
- Demonstrated experience in civil construction and infrastructure projects.
- Experience in planning, coordinating and overseeing civil engineering and construction works.
- Demonstrated ability to interpret and work from engineering drawings, plans, specifications and construction documentation.
- Experience with project cost estimation, quantity measurement, cost control and budget management.
- Experience assessing design changes and managing variations to project scope, cost and construction methodology.
- Strong knowledge of relevant Australian Standards, construction legislation, quality requirements and workplace health and safety obligations.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant engineering/design software.
- White Card and relevant construction qualifications or tickets will be highly regarded.
- Previous experience in a Project Engineer, Site Engineer or Graduate Civil Engineer role will be highly regarded.
Benefits:
- A competitive remuneration package aligned with experience.
- Clear pathways for professional development and internal progression.
- FIFO 2/1 roster, providing work-life balance.
- Employee assistance program.
Doolee is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

We are seeking a Development Engineer to join our Planning Department Services Team. In this role, you will apply your specialist civil engineering knowledge to support and influence the City’s land development process., underpinned by a tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering. You will play a role in coordinating and assessing Structure Plans, Subdivision Plans, Development Applications and Civil Engineering approvals.
To be considered for this role, you must address the following selection criteria as part of your online application:
- Knowledge of planning process and the relevant statutory guidance for Greenfield subdivision and urban infill development sites.
- An ability to perform composite analysis, interpret technical data and consider complex design elements attached to the provision of road and drainage infrastructure.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience in the modelling and implementation of urban water management concepts.
- Knowledge of project management, construction techniques, materials and coordination of civil engineering related works.
- Experience with software packages such as 3D Civil.
- Quality communication (verbal and written) and a high-level negotiation skills.
- Demonstrated experience leading a team.
Please refer to other “Essential Requirements” of the Job, as outlined in the position description which is included in the information package (available from the City of Rockingham Job Vacancies page).
What we offer
This position offers a gross annual salary of $120,603 - $128,590 per annum and:
- 12% superannuation with the option to co-contribute up to a further 5%
- Flexible working arrangements, including rostered days off and two additional paid days of absence per year
- A variety of health and wellbeing programs including a physical health reimbursement subsidy payment of up to $200 per annum, free flu vaccinations, free skin cancer checks, mental health programs and Employee Assistance Provider (EAP) services

If you identify as a person with disability and require adjustments throughout the recruitment and selection process please contact the Recruitment Team via email at jobs@rockingham.wa.gov.au or phone 08 9528 0333. We’re happy to discuss options to assist you e.g. we can provide alternate formats for application forms, or alternate methods of applying. 
The City of Rockingham encourages candidates from a diverse range of backgrounds, including First Nations people, people living with disability and people who speak a first language other than English.

The Role
We're looking for a motivated and technically capable Engineer Dam Infrastructure to join us on a permanent full-time basis. Reporting to the Dam Infrastructure Manager, you'll play a key role in supporting the safe, compliant and efficient management of TasWater's dam infrastructure assets across Tasmania.  
This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to dam safety engineering, asset performance, compliance and continuous improvement initiatives that help protect our communities, environment and critical infrastructure. Working closely with engineers, operators, specialists and external stakeholders, you'll help deliver engineering solutions that support both regulatory obligations and long-term asset outcomes.  
As part of the team, you'll work across TasWater's diverse portfolio of 304 dams, including concrete weirs, earthen embankment dams, and concrete arch and buttress dams. Spread across some of Tasmania's most spectacular and remote locations, these assets offer a rare opportunity to blend engineering expertise with field-based work while helping safeguard critical water infrastructure for future generations. 
In this role, you will: 
- Deliver dam safety engineering support, solutions and improvements to achieve compliance and asset performance outcomes. 
- Provide project management and technical oversight for dam infrastructure programs and improvement works. 
- Monitor and analyse dam asset performance to support asset, workforce and community safety. 
- Research, analyse and report on engineering issues, developing practical and compliant solutions. 
- Schedule and coordinate compliance, surveillance and inspection activities. 
- Prepare and maintain engineering documentation including reports, plans, specifications and business cases. 
- Support emergency preparedness activities, including participation in dam safety emergency exercises. 
- Build effective relationships with operational teams, contractors, consultants and industry stakeholders to achieve organisational outcomes. 
For a full copy of the position description, please visit our website: www.taswater.com.au
What we're looking for
We're seeking an engineering professional who combines sound technical knowledge with strong problem-solving and stakeholder engagement capabilities. 
To thrive in this role, you’ll bring: 
- A degree in Engineering or equivalent demonstrated experience in dam safety asset management functions. 
- A sound understanding of engineering concepts and principles relating to water and sewerage infrastructure. 
- Strong engineering analysis and problem-solving skills. 
- Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills. 
- The ability to interpret technical plans, drawings and specifications. 
- Proficiency in engineering software and computer-based systems. 
- Knowledge of relevant health and safety legislation, regulations and codes of practice. 
- A current Class C driver's licence. 
Highly regarded: 
- Project management experience or qualifications. 
- Full professional membership of a relevant engineering association. 
- White Card (Work Safely in the Construction Industry). 
- Knowledge of relevant Australian and international engineering standards, including ANCOLD Guidelines.

Across our multi-disciplinary organisation, we are serious about enhancing the skills and careers of our team members. When you join TasWater, you join a company that offers career development pathways, training courses, and access to subject matter experts. 
We are continuing to build an inclusive workplace and workforce that truly represents the Tasmanian community that we serve. We value diversity in all its many forms and welcome a range of perspectives and identities to enrich the way we work and what we do. 
We take pride in being acknowledged as an employer of choice for women by WORK180. Visit the Work180 website to view our benefits and policies, such as 18 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents regardless of tenure and with full superannuation contributions. We’re continuing to work on future benefits through a dedicated Employee Experience team. 
The Details
This role can be based either at Hobart, Launceston or Devonport and attracts a salary range of $113,918.64 - $120,247.46 per annum (inclusive of superannuation). 
The position may require travel throughout Tasmania, site inspections, work in both indoor and outdoor environments, and participation in after-hours work or an on-call roster as required to support business operations. 
Ready to apply? Simply include a CV/resume and a 1–2-page cover letter telling us how your experience matches "What we are looking for" and how you connect to our TasWater values and vision.    
If you want to learn more about this role, please contact Gemma Casey - Dam Infrastructure Manager at 0436 624 732 or via email at Gemma.Casey@taswater.com.au  
If you need assistance in applying, please contact Roly Srivastava – Talent Acquisition Officer at 0498 608 719 or via email at Roly.Srivastava@taswater.com.au  
Application will close at 10am on Wednesday, 21st October, 2026.

As part of our recruitment process, you may be asked to participate in pre-employment checks relevant to the role. These may include a National Police Check or AusCheck, with any offer of employment subject to satisfactory outcomes.

candidates.content_text:
The Role
Reporting to the Area Manager – Civil / NPI, you'll support the delivery of civil and non-process infrastructure projects across the Watershed Project and other company developments. You'll coordinate engineering, procurement and construction activities while helping drive safe and efficient project execution
- Coordinating civil construction and infrastructure packages
- Managing contractor and consultant interfaces
- Reviewing designs, drawings and technical documentation
- Supporting construction planning, scheduling and progress reporting
- Monitoring costs, procurement and project performance
- Driving quality assurance, inspections and project handovers
- Promoting strong safety leadership across site activities
About You
We're looking for a proactive Project Engineer who enjoys being part of a team, solving problems and helping projects move forward. To be considered for this position, you will possess the following.
- Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering
- 3 to 7 years' experience in mining, infrastructure or heavy civil projects
- Experience managing contractors and engineering consultants
- Strong understanding of civil earthworks and infrastructure delivery
- Knowledge of roads, drainage, utilities and construction methodologies
- Experience in EPC/EPCM or owner's team environments
- Strong planning, communication and stakeholder management skills
- Willingness to travel regularly to remote project locations
Why Tungsten Mining?
Tungsten Mining (ASX : TGN) is an Australian critical minerals company advancing a portfolio of world-class tungsten assets. Our people are shaping these internationally recognised projects to strengthen, secure and diversify tungsten supply for Australia and its partners across the globe.
Collaborating with an experienced and entrepreneurial team, your expertise, energy and innovation will contribute directly to overall project success and long-term value creation.
Who is Tungsten Mining
Tungsten Mining is an Australian critical minerals company focused on the development of tungsten projects across Australia. Our flagship assets include the globally significant Mt Mulgine Project in Western Australia and the shovel-ready Watershed Project in North Queensland, together forming one of the world’s largest tungsten development portfolios. 
To Apply
If you're looking for a role where you can contribute to the successful delivery of a major mining development, work with experienced project professionals and make a lasting impact on critical infrastructure projects, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today!
Please note: We reserve the right to commence the shortlisting process for this role immediately and the right to remove the advertisement before the closing date.
Agency submissions will not be considered for this position.

candidates.abstract: Seeking a Civil Estimator in Murray Bridge to prepare precise tenders for infrastructure and earthworks projects across South Australia.
candidates.location: Murray Bridge, Riverland & Murray Mallee SA
candidates.content_text:
Civil Construction Estimator | Earthworks & Infrastructure
Location: Murray Bridge & Regional SA
Work Type: Full-time, Permanent
About the Business
Randstad has partnered exclusively with a well-established, family-owned civil construction business based in the Murraylands region of South Australia. Specialising in civil infrastructure, subdivisions, earthworks, and road construction, they are seeking an experienced Civil Construction Estimator to join their management team and drive project growth through accurate tendering.
Key Responsibilities
- Prepare detailed cost estimates and competitive tender submissions for varied civil projects.
- Perform quantity calculations, cost analysis, and constructability assessments.
- Source, evaluate, and negotiate quotes from subcontractors and suppliers.
- Identify project risks, commercial opportunities, and value engineering options.
- Collaborate with clients, consultants, and internal project managers throughout the bidding process.
- Facilitate seamless project handovers to the operations team following successful contract awards.
What You Bring
- Proven experience in civil construction estimating covering earthworks, roads, drainage, and subdivisions.
- Strong ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, contracts, and technical specifications.
- Knowledge of local government and SA Department for Infrastructure and Transport (DIT) tendering processes.
- Excellent numerical, analytical, and computer skills, including proficiency with estimating software.
- Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related discipline are preferred.
What's on Offer
- A high-impact role in a growing, family-owned South Australian business where your work directly shapes the project pipeline.
- Collaborative and supportive work culture alongside an experienced leadership team.
- Long-term career opportunity in the expanding Murraylands region.
To Apply
As Randstad is managing this vacancy on an exclusive basis, all applications will be reviewed with the strictest confidentiality.
To discuss this exclusive opportunity, please contact Ezgi Erdogan-Frost at 0419 381 964 or email your CV to ezgi.erdoganfrost@randstad.com.au
At Randstad, we are passionate about providing equal employment opportunities and embracing diversity to the benefit of all. We actively encourage applications from any background.
